G5200.def:
ὑγρός, -ά, -όν, 
[in LXX: Juges 16:7,8 (לַח), Job 8:16 (רָשׂב), Sir.39:13 
wet, moist, opposite to ξηρός: of wood, sappy, green: Luc 23:31.†

G5201.def:
ὑδρία, -ας, ἠ
(ὕδωρ), [in LXX for בַּד ;] 
__1. prop., a water-pot or jar: Jean 2:6, 7 John 4:28.
__2. More frequently in Attic = ἄγγυς, a pot, urn or jar of any kind, as for holding wine, coins, etc. (see Rutherford, NPhr., 23; MM, xxv).
†

G5202.def:
ὑδροποτίω, -ῶ
(ὕδωρ, πίνω), [in LXX: Dan LXX 1:12 שָׁתָה מַיִם) * ;] 
to drink water, opposite to οἴνῳ χρῆσθαι: 1 Timothée 5:23 (Hdt., i, 71; Plat., Rep., 561 with, al.).†

G5203.def:
ὑδρωπικός, -ή, -όν
(ὕδρωψ, dropsy), 
dropsical, suffering from dropsy: Luc 14:2.†

G5204.def:
ὕδωρ 
genitive, 
ὕδατος, τό, 
[in LXX chiefly for מַיִם ;] 
water: Matthieu 3:16, Marc 1:10, Luc 7:44, Jean 4:7, Jacques 3:12, Apocalypse 8:10, al.; pl., Matthieu 14:28-29, Jean 3:23, Apocalypse 1:15, al.; βαπτίζειν (ἐν) ὕδατι, Matthieu 3:11, Marc 1:8, Jean 1:26, al.; τ. λυυτρὸν τοῦ ὕ., Éphésiens 5:26; opposite to οἴνος, Jean 2:9 4:46; αἷμα, Jean 19:34, Hébreux 9:19, 1 Jean 5:6 Jn 5:8 Matthieu 17:15 Marc 9:22; πνεῦμα, Jean 1:26, 31 1:33; πνεῦμα καὶ πῦρ, Matthieu 3:11, Luc 3:16;ἐξ ὕ. κ. πνεύματος γεννηθῆναι, Jean 3:5; metaphorically, of divine truth and grace (τ.) ὕ. (τ.) ζῶν, Jean 4:10-11 (cf. Jean 4:13-15); τ. ὕ. τ. ζωῆς, of spiritual refresh­ment, Apocalypse 21:6 22:1, 17

G5205.def:
ὑετός, -οῦ, ὁ
(ὕω, to rain), [in LXX chiefly for ;] 
rain: Actes 14:17 28:2, Hébreux 6:7, Jacques 5:18, Apocalypse 11:6; ὄψιμος (which see), sc. ὑ., Jacques 5:7.†

G5206.def:
υἱοθεσία, -ας, ἡ
(cf. the cl. phrases, υἱὸν τίθεσθαι, θετὸς υἱός), frequently in Inscr. (see Deiss., BS, 239), adoption of a son (or daughter); metaphorically, of God's relation established 
__(a) with Israel: Romains 9:4; 
__(b) with Christ­ians: Romains 8:15, Galates 4:5, Éphésiens 1:5; of its consummation, Romains 8:23.†

G5208.def:
ὕλη, -ης, ἡ 
[in LXX: Job 19:29 (†) Job 38:40 (סֻכָּה), Psaumes 69:2 B.l א (יָוֵן), Ésaïe 10:17 (שָׁמִיר), Wis.11:17 15:13, Sir.28:10, 2Ma.2:24, 4Ma.1:29 * ;] 
__1. wood, forest, woodland (Thus., Xen., al.). 
__2. wood, timber, fuel (Hom., Hdt., Thuc., al.): Jacques 3:5 (see Hort, Ja., 70, 104 f.). 
__3. = Lat. materia, esp. in Philosophy, matter (Arist. and later writers; Wis, ll. with).†

G5214.def:
ὑμνέω, -ῶ
(ὕμνος) [in LXX for הָלַל pi., שִׁיר, יָדָה hi., etc. ;] 
__1. trans., with accusative of person(s) (in cl. also with accusative of thing(s)), to sing to, laud, sing to the praise of: Actes 16:25, Hébreux 2:12. 
__2. Intrans., to sing: in LXX and NT, of singing hymns and praises to God (Psaumes 65:13, al.), Matthieu 26:30, Marc 14:26 (see Swete, in l).†

G5217.def:
ὑπ-άγω 
[in LXX: Exode 14:21 (הָלַךְ hi.), elsewhere only as seel., Tob.8:21, al. ;] 
a word of the vulgar language, in Pres. and imperfect only (Bl., § 53, 1). 
__I. Trans. 
__1. to lead or bring under, subdue (Hom., Hdt., al.; Ex, l.with). 
__2. to lead on slowly (Hdt., Xen., al.). 
__II. Intrans., to go slowly away, withdraw oneself, depart (so less frequently in cl.; Thuc., Eur., al.): absol., Matthieu 8:32 13:44, Marc 6:33, Luc 8:42 17:14, Jean 6:67 8:2 11:44 14:5, 28 18:8; οἱ ἐρχόμενοι κ. οἱ ὑπάγοντες, Marc 6:31; ὑπῆγον κ. ἐπίστευον, Jean 12:11; ἵνα ὑπαγῆτε κ. καρπὸν ψέρητε, Jean 15:16; opposite to ἔρχεσθαι, Jean 3:8 8:14; imperat., ὕπαγε, Matthieu 4:10 8:13 20:14, Marc 2:9 T, Marc 7:29 10:52; εἰς εἰρήνην (ἐν εἰ.), Marc 5:34, Jacques 2:16; id. prefixed to another imperat. (Bl., § 79, 4), Matthieu 5:34 8:4 18:15 19:21 21:28 27:65 28:10, Marc 1:44 10:21 16:7, Jean 4:16 9:7, Apocalypse 10:8; with καί inserted, Apocalypse 16:1; euphemistically, of death, Matthieu 26:24, Marc 14:21; with adv.: ποῦ (which see), Jean 12:35 14:5 16:5, 1 Jean 2:11; ὅπου (which see), Jean 8:21-22 13:33, 36 14:4 Apocalypse 14:4; ἐκεῖ, Jean 11:8; with prep.: πρός, Jean 7:33 13:3 16:5, 10 16:17; εἰς, Matthieu 9:6 20:4, 7, Marc 2:11 11:2 14:13, Luc 19:30, Jean 6:21 7:3 9:11 11:31, Apocalypse 13:10 17:8, 11; εἰς . . . πρός, Matthieu 26:18, Marc 5:19; ἐπί, Luc 12:58; μετά, Matthieu 5:41; ὀπίσω, Matthieu 16:23, Marc 8:33; with inf., Jean 21:3.†

G5218.def:
ὑπακοή, -ῆς, ἡ
(ὑπακούω), [in LXX: 2 Rois 22:36 (עֲנָוָה); in Aq.: 2 Rois 23:23 * ;] 
obedience (opposite to παρακοή); 
__1. in general, absol., εἰς ὑ., Romains 6:16; with genitive subjc., 2 Corinthiens 7:15 10:6, Phm 21; with genitive obj., Romains 1:5 (Lft, Notes, 246) Romains 16:26, 1 Pierre 1:22; τ. Χριστοῦ, 2 Corinthiens 10:5. 
__2. Of obedience to God's commands: absol., 1 Pierre 1:2; opposite to ἁμαρτία, Romains 6:16; τέκνα ὑπακοῆς, 1 Pierre 1:14; with genitive subj., Romains 15:18 16:19. 
__3. Of Christ's obedience: absol., Hébreux 5:8; with genitive subj., Romains 5:19. 
(The word is not found except in LXX, NT and eccl.).†

G5219.def:
ὑπακούω 
[in LXX: chiefly for שָׁמַע ;] 
to listen, attend, hence, 
__(a) to answer a knock at a door (Plat., Xen., al.): Actes 12:13; 
__(b) to attend to, submit to, obey (Hdt., Thuc., al.): absol., Philippiens 2:12; with inf., Hébreux 11:8; with dative of person(s) (Plat., al.; but more frequently with genitive), Matthieu 8:27, Marc 1:27 4:41, Luc 8:25 17:6, Romains 6:16, Éphésiens 6:1, 5, Colossiens 3:20, 22, Hébreux 5:9, 1 Pierre 3:6; with dative of thing(s), Actes 6:7, Romains 6:12 10:16, 2 Thessaloniciens 1:8 3:14; before εἰς (by attraction, for dative; see ICC, in l), Romains 6:17.†

G5220.def:
ὕπανδρος, -ον 
[in LXX: Nombres 5:20, 29 (אִישׁ תַּחַת), Proverbes 6:24, 29, Sir.9:9 41:21 * ;] 
under or subject to a man, married: γυνή, Romains 7:2 (Polyb., Diod., al.).†

G5221.def:
ὑπ-αντάω, -ῶ 
[in LXX: Dan LXX 10:14 (קָרָה), Sir.9:3, al. ;] 
to go to meet, meet: with dative of person(s) (see M, Pr., 64), Matthieu 8:28 28:9, Marc 5:2, Luc 8:27 17:12 (ἀπ-, WH, txt.), Jean 4:51 11:20, 30 12:18, Actes 16:16; of meeting in battle, Luc 14:31.†

G5222.def:
ὑπ-άντησις, -εως, ἡ
(ὑπαντάω), [in LXX: Juges 11:34, εἰς ὑ. (קִרְאָה), etc. ;] 
a going to meet: εἰς ὑ. (see M, Proverbes 14:1-35 n), Matthieu 8:34 25:1, Jean 12:13.†

G5223.def:
ὕπαρξις, -εως, ἡ
(ὑπάρχω), [in LXX for רְכוּשׁ, הוֹן, etc. ;] 
__1. subsistence, existence (Arist., al.). 
__2. In late writers, = τὰ ὑπάρχοντα, substance, property: Hébreux 10:34; pl., Actes 2:45.†

G5225.def:
ὑπάρχω 
[in LXX for הָיָה, יֵשׁ, לוּן, etc.; τ. ὑπάρχοντα for מִקְנֶה, רְכוּשׁ, etc. ;] 
__1. to begin, make a beginning (Hom., Hdt., al.). 
__2. to be in existence, be ready, be at hand (Hdt., Thuc., al.): Actes 19:40 27:12, 21; before ἐν, Actes 28:18. 
__3. to be, prop, expressing continuance of an antecedent state or condition (cf. Gifford, Incarnation, 11 ff.; MM, xxv): with, nom, pred., Luc 8:41 9:48, Actes 4:34 7:55 8:16 16:3 19:36 21:20, 1 Corinthiens 7:26 12:22, Jacques 2:15, 2 Pierre 3:11; ptcp. with pred., Luc 16:14 23:50, Actes 2:30, 32 17:24 22:3, Romains 4:19, 1 Corinthiens 2:15, 2 Corinthiens 8:17 12:16, Galates 1:14 2:14; pl., Luc 11:13, Actes 16:20, 37 17:29, 2 Pierre 2:19; before ἐν, with dative of thing(s), Luc 7:25 16:23, Actes 5:4 10:12, 1 Corinthiens 11:18, Philippiens 3:20; ἐν μορφῇ θεοῦ ὑπάρχων (R, mg., being originally), Philippiens 2:6; ἐν, with dative of person(s), (among), 1 Corinthiens 11:18; μακρὰν ἀπό, Actes 17:27; πρὸς τ. σωτηρίας, Actes 27:34. 
__4. to belong to (Thuc., Xen., al.): with dative of person(s), Actes 3:6 4:37 28:7, 2 Pierre 1:8; τὰ ὑπάρχοντα, one's belongings, possessions: with dative of person(s), Luc 8:3 12:15, Actes 4:32; with genitive of person(s), Matthieu 19:21 24:47 25:14, Luc 11:21 12:33, 44 14:33 16:1 19:8, 1 Corinthiens 13:3, Hébreux 10:34 (cf. προ-υπάρχω).†

G5226.def:
ὑπ-είκω 
[in LXX: 4Ma.6:35 * ;] 
__1. to retire, withdraw. 
__2. to yield, submit: metaphorically, Hébreux 13:17.†

G5227.def:
ὑπ-εναντίος, -α, -ον 
[in LXX for אָיַב, צַר, etc. ;] 
set over against, opposite. Metaphorical (Plat., Arist., al.), opposed to, contrary to: with dative of person(s), Colossiens 2:14; absol., as subst., ὁ ὑ., Hébreux 10:27 (cf. Ésaïe 26:11).†

G5228.def:
ὑπέρ (when following subst.—poët.—ὕπερ; so as adv., 2 Corinthiens 11:23), 
prep. with genitive, accusative 
__I. C. genitive, primarily of place (rest or motion), over, above, across, beyond, hence, metaphorically, 
__1. for, on behalf of: of prayer, Matthieu 5:44, Actes 8:24, Romains 10:1, Jacques 5:16, al.; of laying down life, Jean 10:11, Romains 9:3, al.; esp. of Christ giving his life for man's redemption, Marc 14:24, Jean 10:15, Actes 21:13, Romains 5:6-8, al.; opposite to κατά, Marc 9:40, Luc 9:50, Romains 8:31. 
__2. Causal, for, because of, for the sake of: with genitive of person(s), Actes 5:41, Romains 1:5, Philippiens 1:29, 2 Corinthiens 12:10, al.; with genitive of thing(s), Jean 11:4, Romains 15:8, 2 Corinthiens 1:6, al. 
__3. = ἀντί (see M, Pr., 105), for, instead of, in the name of: 1 Corinthiens 15:29, 2 Corinthiens 5:15, 21 Galates 3:13, Colossiens 1:7, Phm 13 (cf. Field, Notes, 225). 
__4. In more colourless sense, = περί (M, Pr., l.with), for, concerning, with regard to: Romains 9:27, 2 Corinthiens 1:6 8:23 12:8, Philippiens 1:7, 2 Thessaloniciens 2:1, al. 
__II. C. accusative, primarily of place, over, beyond, across, hence, metaphorically, of measure or degree in excess, above, beyond, over, more than: Matthieu 10:24, 37 Luc 6:40, Actes 26:13, 1 Corinthiens 10:13, 2 Corinthiens 1:8, Éphésiens 1:22 3:20, Phm 16, al.; after comparatives = than (Juges 11:25, al.), Luc 16:8, Hébreux 4:12. 
__III. As adv. (see supr. ad init.), more: ὕπερ ἐγώ, I more, 2 Corinthiens 11:23; in compounds, see: ὑπεράνω, ὑπερλίαν, ὑπερπερισσῶς. 
__IV. In composition: over (ὑπεραίρω), beyond (ὑπερβάλλω), more (ὐπερνικάω), on behalf of (ὐπερεντυγχάνω).

G5229.def:
ὑπερ-αίρω 
[in LXX: 2 Chroniques 32:23 (נָשָׂא ni.), etc. ;] 
to lift or raise over. Mid., to uplift oneself: 2 Corinthiens 12:7; before ἐπί, with accusative, of person(s), 2 Thessaloniciens 2:4 (cf. 2Ma.5:23).†

G5230.def:
ὑπέρακμος, -ον 
past the bloom of youth: 1 Corinthiens 7:36 (Eustath.).†

G5231.def:
ὑπερ-άνω 
compound adv., [in LXX for עַל, מֵעָל, etc. ;] 
above: as prep. with genitive, Éphésiens 1:21 4:10, Hébreux 9:5.†

G5232.def:
ὑπερ-αυξάνω 
to increase beyond measure: 2 Thessaloniciens 1:3 (see Lft., Notes, 98).†

G5233.def:
ὑπερ-βαίνω 
[in LXX for עָבַר, etc. ;] 
__1. trans., to step over, trans­gress (R, overreach: 1 Thessaloniciens 4:6). 
__2. Intrans., to transgress: metaphorically, 1 Thessaloniciens 4:6 (R, txt.; see M, Th., in l).†

G5234.def:
ὑπερβαλλόντως 
[in LXX: Job 15:11 א B (†) * ;] 
above measure: 2 Corinthiens 11:23.†

G5235.def:
ὑπερ-βάλλω 
[in LXX: Job 15:11 A (†), Sir.5:7 25:11, al. ;] 
__1. trans., to throw over or beyond. 
__2. Intrans., to run beyond. In both senses, metaphorically, to exceed, surpass, transcend: 2 Corinthiens 3:10 9:14, Éphésiens 1:19 2:7; with genitive obj., Éphésiens 3:19.†

G5236.def:
ὑπερ-βολή, -ῆς, ἡ
(ὑπερβάλλω), [in LXX: καθ᾽ ὑ., 4Ma.3:18 * ;] 
a throwing beyond. Metaphorical, excess, superiority, excellence: 2 Corinthiens 4:7 12:7; καθ᾽ ὑπερβολήν, beyond measure, exceedingly, Romains 7:13, 1 Corinthiens 12:31, 2 Corinthiens 1:8, Galates 1:13; κ. ὑ. εἰς ὑ., beyond all measure, 2 Corinthiens 4:17.†

G5237.def:
ὑπερ-εῖδον, aor. 
[in LXX for עָלַם hi., מַעַל, etc. ;] 
to overlook: with accusative of thing(s), Actes 17:30

G5238.def:
ὑπερ-έκεινα 
comp. adv. (see Bl., 28, 2; M, Pr., 99), 
beyond: as prep. with genitive, τὰ ὑ. ὑμῶν, 2 Corinthiens 10:16 (Byz. and Ecclésiaste 1:1-18.).†

G5239.def:
ὑπερ-εκ-τείνω 
to stretch out overmuch: metaphorically, ἑαυτούς, 2 Corinthiens 10:14.†

G5240.def:
ὑπερ-εκ-χύννω (Rec. -ύνω), late form of -χέω 
to pour out over. Pass., to overflow, run over: Luc 6:38 (not elsewhere).†

G5241.def:
ὑπερ-εν-τυγχάνω 
to intercede or make petition for (see Deiss., BS, 121 f.): before ὑπέρ, Romains 8:26.†

G5242.def:
ὑπερ-έχω 
[in LXX: Genèse 25:23 (אָמַץ), Exode 26:13 (עֲדַף), Sir.36:7, al. ;] 
__1. trans., to hold over or above. 
__2. Intrans. (when a noun follows, the case is governed by the prep.; see Bl., § 34, 1; 36, 8), to rise above, overtop; metaphorically, 
__(a) to be superior in rank, etc.: Romains 13:1, 1 Pierre 2:13 (cf. Wis.6:6); 
__(b) to be superior, excel, surpass: with genitive (cl.; see supr.), Philippiens 2:3; with accusative (cl.; see supr.), Philippiens 4:7; as subst., τ. ὑπερέχον, the excel­lency, the surpassing worth, Philippiens 3:8.†

G5243.def:
ὑπερηφανία, -ας, ἡ
(ὑπερήφανος, which see), [in LXX chiefly for גָּאוֹן and cogn. forms ;] 
haughtiness, arrogance, disdain: Marc 7:22 (Plat., Xen.).†

G5245.def:
ὑπερ-νικάω, -ῶ 
[in LXX: Da TH Daniel 6:3; in Sm.: Psaumes 43:1 * ;] 
to be more than conqueror: Romains 8:37 (eccl.).†

G5246.def:
ὑπέρ-ογκος, -ον 
[in LXX: Deutéronome 30:11 (פָּלָא), etc. ;] 
of excessive weight or size; metaphorically, excessive, immoderate, in late writers, of arrogant speech (see Mayor on Ju, l.with): n. pl., 2 Pierre 2:18, Ju 16.†

G5247.def:
ὑπεροχή, -ῆς, ἡ
(ὑπερέχω) [in LXX: Jérémie 52:22 (קוֹמָה), 2Ma.3:11, al. ;] 
a projection, eminence, as the peak of a mountain. Metaphorical (Arist.), excellence, pre-eminence: λόγου ἢ σοφίας, 1 Corinthiens 2:1; οἱ ἐν ὑ (for a parallel to this phrase, see Deiss., BS, 255, and cf. 2Mac, l.with), 1 Timothée 2:2.†

G5248.def:
ὑπερ-περισσεύω 
to abound more exceedingly: Romains 5:21. Mid., in same sense (RV, overflow): with dative of thing(s), 2 Corinthiens 7:4.†

G5250.def:
ὑπερ-πλεονάζω 
to abound exceedingly: 1 Timothée 1:14 (Ps Sol 5:19; Herm., Mand., v, 2, 5).†

G5251.def:
ὑπερ-υψόω, -ῶ 
[in LXX: Psaumes 37:35 (עָרִיץ) Psaumes 97:9 (עָלָה ni.), Da TH Daniel 4:34 11:12 (רוּם), ib. LXX TH Daniel 3:52 ff.* ;] 
__1. to exalt beyond measure, exalt to the highest place: Philippiens 2:9. 
__2. to extol (Da, ll. with).†

G5252.def:
ὑπερ-φρονέω, -ῶ 
[in LXX: 4Ma.13:1 4Mac 14:11 4Mac 16:2 * ;] 
__1. to be overproud, high-minded (Æsch.): μὴ ὑ. παρ᾽ ὃ δεῖ φρονεῖν (on the paranom., see Vau., in l), Romains 12:3. 
__2. to overlook, think slightly of (Thuc., Plat.).†

G5253.def:
ὑπερῷον, -ου, τό 
(neut. of ὑπερῷος, above, ὑπέρ) [in LXX for עֲלִיָּה and cogn. forms ;] 
__1. in cl., the upper story or upper rooms where the women resided (Hom., a1.). 
__2. In LXX and NT, an upper chamber, roof-chamber, built on the flat roof of the house (see DB, iii, 674a): Actes 1:13 9:37, 39 20:8 (cf. 4Ki.23:22).†

G5254.def:
ὑπ-έχω 
[in LXX: Psaumes 89:50 (נָשָׂא), La 5:7 (סָבַל), Wis.12:21, 2Ma.4:48 * ;] 
to hold or put under. Metaphorical, to undergo, suffer: δίκην, Ju 7 (Soph., Eur., al.).†

G5255.def:
ὑπήκοος, -ον
(ὑπακσύω), [in LXX: Jean 17:13 (לָמַם) Proverbes 21:28 (שָׁמַע), etc. ;] 
giving ear, obedient, subject: Philippiens 2:8; with dative of person(s), Actes 7:39; εἰς πάντα, 2 Corinthiens 2:9.†

G5256.def:
ὑπηρετέω, -ῶ
(ὑπηρέτης) [in LXX: Wis.16:21, 24-25 19:6, Sir.39:4 * ;] 
prop., to serve as rower on a ship (Diod., al.). In cl. always metaphorically, to minister to, serve: with dative of person(s), Actes 13:36 20:34 24:23.†

G5257.def:
ὑπηρέτης, -ου, ὁ
(ὑπό + ἐρέτης, a rower) [in LXX: Proverbes 14:35 (עֶבֶד), Wis.6:4, al. ;] 
prop., an under rower; hence, generally, a servant, attendant, minister: of a magistrate's attendant, Matthieu 5:25; of officers of the Synagogue or Sanhedrin, Matthieu 26:58, Marc 14:54, 65, Luc 4:20, Jean 7:32, 45-46 18:3, 12 18:22 19:6, Actes 5:22, 26; of the attendants of kings, οἱ ὑ. οἱ ἑμοί Jean 18:36; of Christian ministers, Actes 13:5 26:16; ὑπηρέται λόγου, Luc 1:2; Χριστοῦ, 1 Corinthiens 4:1; δοῦλοι κ. ὑ., Jean 18:18.†
SYN.: see: διάκονος

G5258.def:
ὕπνος, -ου, ὁ 
[in LXX for שֵׁנָה, חֲלוֹם, etc. ;] 
sleep: Matthieu 1:24, Luc 9:32, Jean 11:13, Actes 20:9; metaphorically, Romains 13:11.†

G5259G.def:
ὑπό (before smooth breathing ὑπ᾽, Matthieu 8:9b, Luc 7:8b; before rough breathing ὑφ᾽, Romains 3:9; on the neglect of elision in Mt, Lk, ll. witha, Galates 3:22, see WH, App., 146; Tdf., Pr., iv), 
prep. with genitive, dative (not in NT), accusative 
__I. C. genitive, primarily of place, under, hence, metaphorically, of the efficient cause, by: after passive verbs, with genitive of person(s), Matthieu 1:22, Marc 1:5, Luc 2:18, Jean 14:21, Actes 4:11, 1 Corinthiens 1:11, Hébreux 3:4, al.; with genitive of thing(s), Matthieu 8:24, Luc 7:24, Romains 3:21, al.; with neut. verbs and verbs with pass, meaning, Matthieu 17:12, Marc 5:26, 1 Corinthiens 10:9, 10 1 Thessaloniciens 2:14, al. 
__II. C. accusative, under; 
__1. of motion: Matthieu 5:15 8:8, Marc 4:21, Luc 13:34; hence, metaphorically, of subjection, Romains 7:14, 1 Corinthiens 15:27, Galates 3:22, 1 Pierre 5:6, al. 
__2. Of position: Jean 1:49, Actes 4:12, Romains 3:13, 1 Corinthiens 10:1, al.; hence, metaphorically, under, subject to, Matthieu 8:9, Romains 3:9, 1 Corinthiens 9:20, Galates 4:5, al. 
__3. Of time, about: Actes 5:21. 
__III. In composition: under (ὑποδέω), hence, of subjection (ὑποτάσσω), compliance (ὑπακούω), secrecy (ὑποβάλλω), diminution (ὑποπνέω).

G5259H.def:
ὑπό (before smooth breathing ὑπ᾽, Matthieu 8:9b, Luc 7:8b; before rough breathing ὑφ᾽, Romains 3:9; on the neglect of elision in Mt, Lk, ll. witha, Galates 3:22, see WH, App., 146; Tdf., Pr., iv), 
prep. with genitive, dative (not in NT), accusative 
__I. C. genitive, primarily of place, under, hence, metaphorically, of the efficient cause, by: after passive verbs, with genitive of person(s), Matthieu 1:22, Marc 1:5, Luc 2:18, Jean 14:21, Actes 4:11, 1 Corinthiens 1:11, Hébreux 3:4, al.; with genitive of thing(s), Matthieu 8:24, Luc 7:24, Romains 3:21, al.; with neut. verbs and verbs with pass, meaning, Matthieu 17:12, Marc 5:26, 1 Corinthiens 10:9, 10 1 Thessaloniciens 2:14, al. 
__II. C. accusative, under; 
__1. of motion: Matthieu 5:15 8:8, Marc 4:21, Luc 13:34; hence, metaphorically, of subjection, Romains 7:14, 1 Corinthiens 15:27, Galates 3:22, 1 Pierre 5:6, al. 
__2. Of position: Jean 1:49, Actes 4:12, Romains 3:13, 1 Corinthiens 10:1, al.; hence, metaphorically, under, subject to, Matthieu 8:9, Romains 3:9, 1 Corinthiens 9:20, Galates 4:5, al. 
__3. Of time, about: Actes 5:21. 
__III. In composition: under (ὑποδέω), hence, of subjection (ὑποτάσσω), compliance (ὑπακούω), secrecy (ὑποβάλλω), diminution (ὑποπνέω).

G5261.def:
ὑπογραμμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(ὑπογράφω, (a) to write under; (b) to trace letters for copying), [in LXX: 2Ma.2:28 * ;] 
__1. a writing-copy, hence, 
__2. an example: 1 Pierre 2:11 (Philo).†

G5262.def:
ὑπό-δειγμα, -τος, τό
(ὑποδείκνυμι), [in LXX: Eze.42:15, Sir.44:16, 2Ma.6:28 2Mac 6:31, 4Ma.17:23 * ;] 
used by later writers (Xen. onwards) for παράδειγμα (see Rutherford, NPhr., 62), 
__(a) a figure, copy: Hébreux 8:5 9:23; 
__(b) an example: for imitation, Jean 13:15, Jacques 5:10; for warning, Hébreux 4:11, 2 Pierre 2:6.†
SYN.: ὁμοίωμα, τύπος, ὑποτύπωσις (see DB, iii. 696b)

G5263.def:
ὑπο-δείκνυμι 
[in LXX for נָגַד hi., etc. ;] 
__1. to show secretly. 
__2. to show by tracing out; hence, generally, to teach, make known: with dative of person(s), Luc 6:47 12:5, Actes 9:16; id. with inf., Matthieu 3:7, Luc 3:7; before, ὅτι, Actes 20:35.†

G5264.def:
ὑπο-δέχομαι 
[in LXX: Tob.7:8-9 Jdth.13:13 A, 1Ma.16:15, 4Ma.13:17 * ;] 
to receive under one's roof, receive as a guest, entertain hospitably: with accusative of person(s), Luc 19:6, Actes 17:7, Jacques 2:25; εἰς τ. οἶκον, Luc 10:38 (see MM, xxv).†

G5266.def:
ὑπόδημα, -τος, τό
(ὑποδέω), [in LXX for נָעַל ;] 
a sole bound under the foot, a sandal: Matthieu 3:11 10:10, Marc 1:7, Luc 3:16 10:4 15:22 22:35, Jean 1:27; τ. ποδῶν, Actes 7:33 (LXX) Actes 13:25.†
SYN.: σανδάλιον, q.v

G5267.def:
ὑπόδικος, -ον 
brought to trial, answerable to: with dative of person(s), τ. θεῷ, Romains 3:19 (see MM, xxv).†

G5268.def:
ὑπο-ζύγιος, -α, -ον 
[in LXX for חֲמוֹר ;] 
under the yoke; as subst., τ . (Hdt., al.), a beast of burden; colloq., an ass (see Deiss., BS, 160 f.), and so always in LXX and NT: Matthieu 21:5 (LXX), 2 Pierre 2:16.†

G5269.def:
ὑπο-ζώννυμι 
[in LXX: 2Ma.3:19 * ;] 
to undergird (Hdt., al.; ὑπὸ τ. μάστους, 2Mac, l.with); of a ship, to undergird or frap: Actes 27:17 (see DB, ext. 367a).†

G5270.def:
ύπο-κάτω comp. adv. (see M, Pr., 99), 
[in LXX chiefly for תַּחַת ;] 
below, under: as prep. with genitive, Matthieu 22:44, Marc 6:11 7:28 12:36 (Rec., R, txt., ὑποπόδιον, as in LXX), Luc 8:16, Jean 1:51, Hébreux 2:8" (LXX), Apocalypse 5:3, 13 6:9 12:1.†

G5271.def:
ὑπο-κρίνομαι 
[in LXX: (Job 40:2) אּ1 (AB אּ2 ἀπο-, עָנָה), Sir.1:29 35:15 (32:15) Sir.36:2 (33:2), 2Ma.5:25 2Mac 6:21 2Mac 6:24, 4Ma.6:15 4Mac 6:17 * ;] 
__1. = Att.. ἀποκρίνομαι (which see), to answer, reply (Hom., Hdt., al.). 
__2. to answer on the stage, play apart (Arist., al.). Metaphorical, to feign, pretend (Demos., Polyb.): with accusative and inf., Luc 20:20 (cf. Ps sol 4:22).†

G5272.def:
ὑπό-κρισις, -εως, ἡ
(ὑποκρίνομαι, which see) [in LXX: 2Ma.6:25 * ;] 
__1. a reply, answer (Hdt.). 
__2. play-acting (Arist., Polyb., al.). Metaphorical, pretence, hypocrisy: Matthieu 23:28, Marc 12:15, Luc 12:1, Galates 2:13, 1 Timothée 4:2, 1 Pierre 2:1 (Polyb., Pss Cantique des cantiques 4:7).†

G5273.def:
ὑπο-κριτής, -οῦ, ὁ
(ὑποκρίνομαι, which see) [in LXX Job 34:30 36:13 (חָנֵף) * ;] 
__1. one who answers, an interpreter (Plat.). 
__2. a stage player, actor (Plut., Xen., al.). Metaphorical (in LXX and NT), a pretender, dissembler, hypocrite: Matthieu 6:2, 5 6:16 7:5 15:7 22:18 23:13-15 24:51, Marc 7:6 Luc 6:42 12:56 13:15.†

G5274.def:
ὑπο-λαμβάνω 
[in LXX: Job 2:4 4:1 and frequently (עָנָה), Psaumes 48:9 (דָּמָה pi.), Tob.6:17, Wis.17:2, 3Ma.3:8 3Mac 3:11, al. ;] 
__1. to take or bear up (by supporting from beneath): with accusative of person(s), Actes 1:9. 
__2. to receive, welcome, entertain (Xen.): III Jn 8. 
__3. to catch up in speech (Hdt., al.; Jb, ll. with): Luc 10:30. 
__4. Of mental action, to assume, suppose (Xen., al.; To, Wis, 3Mac, ll. with): Actes 2:15; before ὅτι (see Bl., § 70, 2), Luc 7:43.†

G5275.def:
ὑπο-λείπω 
[in LXX chiefly (pass.) for יָתַר ni., שָׁאַר ni. ;] 
to leave remaining (Hom., Thuc., al.): pass., of survivors, Romains 11:3.†

G5276.def:
ὑπολήνιον, -ου, τό
(ὑπό, ληνός), [in LXX: Joël 3:13 (4:13), Aggée 2:17, (16), Zacharie 14:10, Ésaïe 16:10 (יֶקֶב) * ;] 
a vessel or trough beneath a winepress to receive the juice (RV, a pit for the winepress): Marc 12:1 (see Swete, in l, and cf. ληνός).†

G5277.def:
ὑπο-λιμτάνω 
collat. form of ὑπολείπω, 
to leave behind: 1 Pierre 2:21.†

G5278.def:
ὑπο-μένω 
[in LXX chiefly for קָוָה, also for יָחַל hi., etc. ;] 
__1. in-trans., to stay behind: before ἐν, Luc 2:43; ἐκεῖ, Actes 17:14. 
__2. Trans., 
__(a) with accusative, to await, wait for: Romains 8:24 (Hom., Hdt., Xen., al.); 
__(b) of things, to bear patiently, endure: absol., Matthieu 10:22 24:13, Marc 13:13, 2 Timothée 2:12, Jacques 5:11, 1 Pierre 2:20; τ. θλίψει (dative of circumstance), Romains 12:12; before εἰς, Hébreux 12:7; with accusative of thing(s), 1 Corinthiens 13:7, 2 Timothée 2:10, Hébreux 10:32 12:2-3, Jacques 1:12.†
SYN.: μακροθυμέω (see: ὑπομονή)

G5279.def:
ὑπο-μιμνήσκω 
[in LXX: 3Ki.4:3 B ( hi.), Wis.12:1 18:22, 4Ma.18:14 * ;] 
to cause one to remember, put one in mind or remind one of: with accusative of thing(s), 2 Timothée 2:14, 3Jn.10; with dupl. accusative (Thus., al.), Jean 14:26; with accusative of person(s), before περί, 2 Pierre 1:12; id., before ὅτι, Ju 5; with inf., Tite 3:1; pass., with genitive of thing(s), Luc 22:61.†

G5280.def:
ὑπόμινησις, -εως, ἡ
(ὑπομιμνήσκω) [in LXX: Psaumes 71:6 א (תְּהִלָּה), Wis.16:11, 2Ma.6:17 * ;] 
a reminding, reminder: ἐν ὑ., 2 Pierre 1:13 3:1; with genitive, 2 Timothée 1:5.†

G5281.def:
ὑπο-μονή, -ῆς, ἡ
(ὑπομένω) [in LXX for מִקְוֶה and cogn. forms; frequently in 4Mac ;] 
__1. a remaining behind (Arist.). 
__2. patient enduring, endurance: Luc 8:15 21:19, Romains 5:3-4 15:4-5, 2 Corinthiens 6:4 12:12, Colossiens 1:11, 2 Thessaloniciens 1:4, 1 Timothée 6:11, 2 Timothée 3:10, Tite 2:2, Hébreux 10:36, Jacques 1:3-4 5:11, 2 Pierre 1:6, Apocalypse 2:2-3, 19 13:10 14:12; δι᾽ ὑπομονῆς, Romains 8:25, Hébreux 12:1; with genitive of person(s), 2 Thessaloniciens 3:5 (ICC, in l), Apocalypse 3:10; with genitive of thing(s), Romains 2:7, 2 Corinthiens 1:6, 1 Thessaloniciens 1:3; before ἐν, Apocalypse 1:9.†
SYN.: see: μακροθυμία, and cf. Hort on Jacques 1:3

G5282.def:
ὑπο νοέω, -ῶ 
[in LXX: Da TH Daniel 7:25 (סְבַר), Tob.8:16, Jdth.14:14, Sir.23:21 * ;] 
to suspect, conjecture: Actes 25:18; with accusative and inf., Actes 13:25 27:27.†

G5283.def:
ὑπόνοια, -ας, ἡ
(ὑπονοέω), [in LXX: Dan LXX 4:16, 32 5:6 (רַעְיוֹן), Sir 3:34* ;] 
a suspicion: 1 Timothée 6:4.†

G5284.def:
ὑπο-πλέω 
to sail under, i.e. under the lee of: with accusative, Actes 27:4, 7.†

G5285.def:
ὑπο-πνέω 
__1. to blow underneath (Arist.). 
__2. to blow gently: Actes 27:13.†

G5286.def:
ὑποπόδιον, -ου, τό
(ὑπό, πούς), [in LXX: Psaumes 99:5 110:1, Ésaïe 66:1, La 2:1 (הֲדֹם) * ;] 
a footstool (= cl. θρᾶνος): Jacques 2:3; metaphorically, Matthieu 5:35, Marc 12:36 (ὑποκάτω, WH, R, mg.), Luc 20:43, Actes 2:35 7:49, Hébreux 1:13 10:13 (all, except Mt, l.with, from LXX, Psaumes 110:1, Ésaïe 66:1) (for exx., see Deiss., BS, 223).†

G5287.def:
ὑπό-στασις, -εως, ἡ
(ὑφίστημι, to set under, stand under, support) [in LXX for מַצָּב (1 Rois 13:23 14:4 B), תִּקְוָה (Ruth 1:12, Eze.19:5), etc., also in Wis.16:21 ;] 
__1. a support, base or foundation (in various senses). 
__2. substance (Arist., al.; opposite to φαντασία, ἔμφασις): Hébreux 1:3 
__3. steadiness, firmness (Polyb., al.), hence, assurance, confidence: 2 Corinthiens 9:4 11:17, Hébreux 3:14 11:1 (here perhaps title-deed, as that which gives reality or guarantee; see MM, xxv).†

G5288.def:
ὑπο-στέλλω 
[in LXX: Deutéronome 1:17 (גּוּר), Job 13:8 (נָשָׂא פָּנִים), Habacuc 2:4 (עָפַל pu.), Aggée 1:10 (כָּלָא), Exode 23:21, Wis.6:7, 3Ma.5:28 * ;] 
__1. to draw in, let down (ἱστίον, οὐράν, etc.). 
__2. to draw back, withdraw: ἑαυτόν, Galates 2:12 (Polyb., al.; see Lft., in l). Mid., to shrink or draw back: Hébreux 10:38 (LXX); before τοῦ, with inf., Actes 20:27; οὐδέν, Actes 20:20.†

G5289.def:
ὑπο-στολή, -ῆς, ἡ
(ὑποστέλλω), 
__1. a letting down, lowering (Plut.). 
__2. a shrinking back (Hesych.): οὐκ ἐσμὲν ὑποστολῆς (on the genitive, see Bl., § 35, 2), Hébreux 10:39.†

G5290.def:
ὑπο-στρέφω 
[in LXX chiefly for שׁוּב ], 
__1. trans., to turn back or about (Hem.). 
__2. Intrans., to turn back, return: Luc 2:20, 43 8:37, 40 9:10 10:17 17:15 19:12 23:48, 56, Actes 8:28; with inf., Luc 17:18; before διά, Actes 20:3; εἰς, Luc 1:56 2:45 4:14 7:10 8:3 9:8 11:24 24:33, 52, Actes 1:12 8:25 13:13, 34 14:21 21:6 22:17 23:32, Galates 1:17; ἀπό, Luc 4:1 24:9, Hébreux 7:1; ἐκ, Actes 12:25, 2 Pierre 2:21.†

G5291.def:
ὑπο-στρωννύω 
[in LXX: Ésaïe 58:5 (יָצָא hi.), etc. ;] 
late form of ὑπο-στορέννυμι, to spread or strew under: with accusative of thing(s), Luc 19:36.†

G5292.def:
ὑπο-ταγή, -ῆς, ἡ 
[in LXX: Wis.18:16 A * ;] 
subjection: 2 Corinthiens 9:13, Galates 2:5. 1 Timothée 2:11 3:4.†

G5293.def:
ὑπο-τάσσω 
[in LXX for דָבַר hi., דָּמַם, שׂוּם, שִׁית, etc. ;] 
__1. as a military term, to place or rank under (Polyb.). 
__2. to subject, put in subjection: 1 Corinthiens 15:27, Philippiens 3:21, Hébreux 2:5, 8; pass., Romains 8:20, 1 Corinthiens 15:27-28, 1 Pierre 3:22, Éphésiens 1:22. Mid., to subject oneself, obey: absol., Romains 13:5, 1 Corinthiens 14:34; with dative of person(s), Luc 2:51 10:17, 20, Romains 8:7 10:3 13:1, 1 Corinthiens 14:32 15:28 (ὑποταγήσεται; cf. M, Pr., 163), 1 Corinthiens 16:16, Éphésiens 5:21-22 (T, WH, txt., R, om.), Éphésiens 5:24, Colossiens 3:18, Tite 2:5, 9 3:1, Hébreux 12:9, 1 Pierre 2:18 3:1 3:5 5:5; imperat., Jacques 4:7, 1 Pierre 2:13 5:5.†

G5294.def:
ὑπο-τίθημι 
[in LXX for שׂוּם, etc. ;] 
to place under, lay down. Metaphorical, τ. τράχηλον ὑποθεῖναι, to risk one's life (see Deiss., LAE, 119 f.): Romains 16:4; mid., to suggest: 1 Timothée 4:6.†

G5295.def:
ὑπο-τρέχω 
to run in under; of navigators, to run in the lee of: with accusative (see M, Pr., 65), Actes 27:16.†

G5296.def:
ὑπο-τύπωσις, -εως, ἡ
(ὑποτυπόω, to delineate), 
an outline, sketch. Metaphorical, a pattern, example: 1 Timothée 1:16, 2 Timothée 1:13.†
SYN.: ὁμοίωμα, τύπος, ὑπόδειγμα (see DB, iii, 696b)

G5297.def:
ὑπο-φέρω 
[in LXX for נָשָׂא, etc. ;] 
to bear by being under. Metaphorical, to endure: with accusative of thing(s), 1 Corinthiens 10:13, 2 Timothée 3:11, 1 Pierre 2:19.†

G5298.def:
ὑπο-χωρέω 
[in LXX: Juges 20:37 B (-), Sir.13:9, 2Ma.12:12 * ;] 
to go back, retire: before ἐν, Luc 5:16; before εἰς, Luc 9:10.†

G5299.def:
ὑπωπιάζω
(ὑπώπιον, (a) the part of the face below the eyes; (b) a blow on the face), 
to strike under the eye, give a black eye: 
metaphorically, 
__(a) of persistent annoyance (RV, wear out), Luc 18:6; 
__(b) of severe self-discipline (R, txt. buffet, mg. bruise), 1 Corinthiens 9:27 (see Field, Notes, 71, 174).†
ὑπο-πιάζω, 
later form of ὑποπιέζω, to press slightly; metaphorically, 
to repress: 1 Corinthiens 9:27 T.7 for ὑπωπιάζω, which see†
